def schedule_talks(capacities, allowed):
    """Assign speakers to talk slots, maximizing how many speakers get scheduled.

    There are m slots; capacities[j] (an int >= 0) is how many speakers slot j
    can hold. There are n speakers, numbered 0..n-1; allowed[i] is a list of
    distinct slot indices (each in range(m), possibly empty) where speaker i
    is willing to talk. A schedule assigns each chosen speaker to one slot
    from their allowed list, never exceeding any slot's capacity.

    Return a tuple (k, scheduled) where k is the maximum possible number of
    scheduled speakers, and scheduled is the sorted list of the speaker
    indices in the schedule achieving that maximum whose sorted index list is
    lexicographically smallest (this optimal set is unique). Note k ==
    len(scheduled). If no speaker can be scheduled, return (0, []).

    Bounds: 0 <= n <= 60, 0 <= m <= 30, 0 <= capacities[j] <= 10.

    >>> schedule_talks([1, 1], [[0], [0], [0, 1]])
    (2, [0, 2])
    >>> schedule_talks([1, 1], [[0, 1], [0]])
    (2, [0, 1])
    >>> schedule_talks([2], [[0], [0], [0]])
    (2, [0, 1])
    """
